idea: A meal-prep subscription app for medical residents who have no time to cook during long hospital shifts.

final_schema.proposed_solution: A meal-prep subscription app for medical residents.
final_schema.target_persona: Medical residents working long hospital shifts.

_regression_note: The topic-drift fixture (gap-closing plan Stage 6). ev-9/ev-10 are freelancer/gig-economy noise -- the exact vocabulary the old SECTION_PREFERENCES dict was hand-tuned on, tested here to confirm a healthcare idea's own evidence isn't penalized for lacking it, and that the noise itself doesn't outrank genuinely relevant healthcare evidence just by accident.

evidence_items.quote: A 2024 survey found 78 percent of medical residents report skipping meals during hospital shifts due to lack of time to cook or shop for groceries.
Most teaching hospitals already operate 24/7 cafeterias offering discounted meals to residents, reducing the urgency of a paid subscription service.
No existing meal-prep service specifically targets the unpredictable, rotating shift schedules that define residency programs.
Three well-funded meal-kit startups targeting healthcare workers have shut down in the past two years, citing thin margins and high customer acquisition costs.
Prepared-meal delivery services are subject to state food-safety licensing requirements that vary significantly by jurisdiction.
ACGME rules cap resident duty hours at 80 per week, but shift timing remains unpredictable across specialties.
Freelance developers on Upwork and Fiverr report growing competition from low-cost overseas bidders on job boards, squeezing hourly rates for client work.
A Telegram bot automation tool for monitoring Discord job postings has attracted a niche audience of freelance automation enthusiasts.
